raw_response:
I’m farming 20 mu of cotton this year, same as I’ve done for many years. With only two people at home, I can’t spread myself too thin, so I’ll keep all the land in cotton instead of trying something new. Cotton takes work, but I know it well, and with the well I can manage if spring is dry. I don’t read those technical recommendations, so I go by what I’ve seen in my own fields and what other women and men around here do. If I put too little fertilizer, the cotton stays weak and doesn’t set well, so I’d rather spend a bit more there, but I still have to watch cash. I’ll plant around mid to late April, use the seed I can buy locally, put most fertilizer in before or at planting, then add a bit later if the plants look short or pale. I’ll irrigate a couple of times if rain doesn’t come, and I’ll spray only when I see weeds or insects getting serious. For tillage, I’ll do the usual plowing and leveling before sowing. Most of the work is still our own hands, and if picking gets too busy, I may hire a few days.
